newsitem.title: ECUADOR: ECUADOR'S CONGRESS APPROVES TELEPHONE FIRM SALE.
newsitem.headline: ECUADOR'S CONGRESS APPROVES TELEPHONE FIRM SALE.

text.p: Ecuador's Congress on Wednesday approved the final amended bill to privatize 35 percent of state telecommunications company Emetel.

"The bill was approved with a majority. Only the Pachakutik, Popular Democratic Movement and Roldosista parties opposed, arguing that the sale would lead to a monopolistic situation," a Congress spokesman said.
Bids in the tender are due in the middle of October.
The amended bill introduced changes to the original law proposed under the former government of President Abdala Bucaram.
The changes introduced would allow one international operator to run both companies into which Emetel will be split, Andinatel and Pacifictel.
The government says Emetel is worth about $1.2 billion.
